newsitem.title: USA: Panel to suggest privatized S. Security - US Senator.
newsitem.headline: Panel to suggest privatized S. Security - US Senator.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said a report to be released Monday by a federal advisory panel increases the odds that Congress will move to privatize part of the Social Security program.
A deeply divided 13-member panel will release three separate plans for ensuring the long-term solvency of the federally-funded retirement program.

Proposals range from having the government invest part of the Social Security trust fund in private markets to setting up compulsory savings accounts, with individuals deciding how to invest part of their Social Security retirement funds.

"For the first time ever, all members of a Social Security advisory council .... have recommended that some of Social Security's funds be invested in the private marketplace to improve return on Social Security funds," Roth, a Delaware Republican, said in a statement.
"This is a very important development and greatly increases the chance that Congress will adopt some kind of investment option," he said.

Beginning in 2012 payroll taxes will no longer cover seniors' benefits under the program. By the year 2030 the Social Security trust fund will run a deficit, unless Congress makes changes in the system.
